notes.meaning: True faith in Jesus as the promised Messiah shows that a person has been given new spiritual life by God. When someone loves God the Father, they naturally love all of God's other children as well. Trusting in Christ brings us into God's family, creating a shared bond of love among all believers.

We can tell that our love for other Christians is real when our hearts are devoted to God and we obey His laws. Genuine love for our brothers and sisters does not come from selfish motives or mere friendship, but from honoring God first. Loving God and loving His people always go hand in hand.

Loving God is not just a warm feeling; it is shown by actively obeying what He tells us to do. His commands are not a crushing burden to those who have been spiritually reborn, because love makes obedience a joy rather than a heavy chore. God also gives His people the inner strength to walk in His ways.

Everyone who receives new life from God has the power to triumph over the evil influences, pressures, and temptations of this fallen world. The tool that wins this victory is our faith. By trusting in Christ, believers rely on His power rather than their own human strength.

No one can truly defeat the corrupting pull of the world except the person who trusts that Jesus is the divine Son of God. Worldly people are ruled by worldly values, but a believer is joined to Jesus, who has already overcome the world. Looking to Christ gives us the hope of heaven and frees our hearts from worldly desires.

Jesus was publicly revealed as the Savior through both water and blood, pointing to His baptism at the start of His ministry and His death on the cross at the end. He did not come only to teach purity, but to shed His blood to take away our sins. The Holy Spirit confirms this truth with absolute certainty because the Spirit cannot lie.

differ.view: Some understand the water and blood to point to the two gospel sacraments, baptism and the Lord's Supper, through which Christ continually ministers cleansing and pardon.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Latin church fathers often saw the water and blood as a reference to the physical flow from Christ's pierced side on the cross, representing the birth of the church and its sacraments.

notes.meaning: A complete and reliable testimony on earth is given by three witnesses: the Holy Spirit, the water of baptism, and the blood shed on the cross. All three point to the exact same truth: that Jesus is the Son of God and the only Savior. Together they give believers a firm basis for trusting the gospel.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Most modern textual scholars regard the extra words mentioning the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit in heaven as a later Latin note that was eventually copied into later manuscripts.

notes.meaning: People accept the testimony of human witnesses every day in courts and ordinary business, so God's testimony is far more worthy of our trust. God is completely wise and cannot lie, making His word infinitely greater than human words. The evidence He has given about His Son settles the matter beyond any doubt.

Whoever trusts in the Son of God experiences God's testimony working personally within their own heart, bringing deep peace and new life. In contrast, anyone who refuses to believe God's message treats the Lord as if He were a liar. Rejecting Christ is an insult to God, because it denies what He has publicly verified about His Son.

The core message God has given us is that He has freely gifted us with eternal life. This everlasting life is not found in our own good works or rituals, but is stored up entirely in His Son, Jesus Christ. To receive this life, a person must be united to Christ through faith.

Anyone who possesses Jesus by faith already has true spiritual life that will last forever. On the other hand, anyone who does not have the Son remains dead in their sins and cut off from God's favor. Eternal life cannot be separated from Jesus, because He is the only source of it.

John explains his primary reason for writing this letter to believers: he wants them to have full, confident assurance that they possess eternal life. God does not want His children to live in constant doubt, but to know their salvation is secure in Christ. This clear knowledge also encourages believers to keep on trusting Jesus every day.

Because believers are children of God, they can approach Him in prayer with bold confidence. God promises to hear our requests whenever we ask for things that line up with His holy will and purposes. This boundary protects us, ensuring that we only receive what God knows is truly good for us.

Knowing that God hears our prayers gives us full confidence that our requests will be answered. Even if we do not see the physical answer right away, we can rest assured that God has granted the petition according to His perfect wisdom and timing. Faith treats God's promises as already secure.

Believers are urged to pray for a fellow Christian who falls into sin, and God will graciously grant life and restoration in answer to that prayer. However, there is a sin that leads to death, such as total, willful rejection of Christ and the Spirit, for which John does not promise answered prayer. While we should pray for others, we must recognize that persistent rebellion against God's truth brings fatal judgment.

differ.view: Some read the sin leading to death as a severe case of backsliding where God chooses to end a believer's earthly physical life as a discipline while still having mercy on the soul.
The sin leading to death is understood as total apostasy or the unpardonable sin against the Holy Spirit, committed by false professors who completely turn away from the gospel.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: This verse has traditionally been used to support the difference between venial sins, which do not destroy the soul's life of grace, and mortal sins, which cause spiritual death.

notes.meaning: Any failure to do what is right according to God's standard is genuine sin. Yet not every sin is an unpardonable offense that leads to final destruction. Christians can take comfort knowing that God provides real forgiveness and cleansing for their daily struggles and shortcomings.

A person who is truly born of God does not make a settled habit of living in unrepentant sin. Jesus Christ, the Son of God, actively guards and protects the believer, and Satan cannot lay a fatal hold on them. Though Christians may slip, God's new nature in them keeps them from completely surrendering to the devil.

Christians have the assurance that they belong to God and have been rescued by His grace. In stark contrast, the rest of the unbelieving world rests helpless and asleep under the dominion and control of Satan. Recognizing this sharp divide reminds believers to stay separate from the world's corrupt ways.

The Son of God has come in human flesh and has given believers spiritual eyes to know the one true God. By being united to His Son Jesus Christ, we are joined to God Himself. Jesus Christ is truly God and the source of eternal life.

John closes his letter with an affectionate warning to guard our hearts against all false gods and images. An idol is anything—whether a carved statue, money, pleasure, or self—that takes the place of honor and worship belonging only to God. Believers must center their complete love and trust on the true God alone.
